learnSection.subtitle: Explore the history, tools, and ethics behind the practice.

topics.title: History of Spellwork
topics.body: Spellwork draws from folk magic, ceremonial traditions, and indigenous practices spanning thousands of years. Modern Wicca, popularized in the mid-20th century by Gerald Gardner, synthesized many of these threads — though witchcraft itself predates any single tradition. Practices vary widely across cultures and should be approached with respect for their origins.

topics.title: Common Tools & Their Roles
topics.body: Candles represent elemental fire and focused intention. Herbs carry traditional correspondences rooted in folk medicine and sympathetic magic. Crystals are used for their symbolic associations rather than proven physical properties. Sigils are personal symbols charged with meaning. None of these tools are required — intention and attention are the foundation of any practice.

topics.title: Ethics & Consent
topics.body: Most contemporary witchcraft traditions emphasize personal responsibility and the importance of consent. Spells intended to influence another person without their knowledge raise ethical questions many practitioners take seriously. The Wiccan Rede — 'An it harm none, do what ye will' — reflects a widely held principle, though interpretations vary. Reflect on your intentions before beginning any working.

topics.title: Safety & Practical Notes
topics.body: Never leave candles unattended. Keep flames away from flammable materials, children, and pets. Some herbs are toxic if ingested or cause skin irritation — research any plant before handling. LED candles and battery-operated alternatives work equally well for most rituals. Spellful offers safe alternatives throughout the library. Spiritual practice is not a substitute for medical, legal, or professional advice.
